papers.boundaryReview: Q2(b)(i) gives 5 each to the two weight diagrams and the pulley diagram, so three tasks. Q3(b)(i) velocities and Q5(a)(i) speeds each share a final 5, so their pairs stay together with shared equations. Q1(c) overtaking times, Q7(a)(ii) launch angles and Q9(i) recurrence values each share a final placement. Q8(a)(i) is one 30-mark Bellman table and optimal plan, not alternative route choices. Q10(a)(i) early/late times share one 20-mark scale. Q10(a)(iv) change to critical paths and completion time shares one 5-mark explanation. Required method steps are not standalone tasks.

papers.markingGuideNote: Use the published scale where printed. Other placements allow 2 for a partially correct element. Deduct 3 for a mathematical error, or 1 for a slip or minor misreading; do not deduct an error twice. Specific table/edge deduction rules and algorithm-naming exceptions take precedence. Alternative valid methods are accepted.
papers.boundaryReview: Q5(a)(ii) has independently marked matrix calculation and interpretation, 5 each. Q8(b)(i) gives 5 to each force diagram. Q3(a)(i) three table values share one 5. Q4(iii) paired times, Q7(v) paired impulses and Q10(a)(i) paired roots each share a final placement. Q8(a)(iii) is one reasoned judgement (5 for supporting friction calculation and 5 for the conclusion), not an independent request to calculate friction. Q9(i) is one 10-mark table with one-mark deductions, and Q6(a)(i) one 10-mark network with edge deductions. The graph entries are required, not finite choices. Q5(b) Bellman route and distance share one 25-mark scale.
